question: Should QQBot permanently reject inbound gateway messages above 16 MiB despite the absence of a published QQ inbound maximum?
rationale: The mechanism is correct and well-proven, but choosing the permanent ceiling intentionally trades memory protection against possible message rejection and reconnect loops; repository evidence cannot determine QQ's maximum legitimate event size.

options.title: Accept the 16 MiB ceiling
options.body: Adopt the conservative channel precedent and substantial JSON-event headroom as the supported QQBot operational policy.

options.title: Require vendor-bound sizing
options.body: Hold the PR until a QQ specification, SDK behavior, or representative production capture supports a different maximum.

options.title: Pause the hard ceiling
options.body: Leave the dependency default unchanged if maintainers judge unknown delivery compatibility more important than the memory bound.

recommendation.title: Accept the 16 MiB ceiling
recommendation.body: Adopt the conservative channel precedent and substantial JSON-event headroom as the supported QQBot operational policy.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current QQBot gateway architecture and are the strongest history-backed owner for its transport policy.
